fieldValues.title: Cluster, domain and boundary are names for one thing
fieldValues.decision_question: Are a cluster, a domain and a boundary different kinds of thing?
fieldValues.context: Boundary and domain were ruled one thing on 2026-10-22 (clerk#129) and reaffirmed on 2026-11-03 (9ee01ac1). On 2026-11-07 the owner said a cluster is probably just another one (38eaff50, 2ad1b8d8). Split from 4a67caf5 on 2026-11-27 so that the part settled by precedent stands apart from the new identity-record fields.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: (a) Keep separate types for domain, boundary and cluster and reconcile their fields: keeps the duplicates and contradicts the ruling. (b) One type with the union of all fields: forces fields no practice has asked for. (c) One thing, a container with an identity record, with cluster, domain and boundary as names (tags) used in different practices: what the ruling already holds, extended to cluster.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Follows the rulings of 2026-10-22 and 2026-11-03. A practice that needs its own fields (muSrs's authority_basis and revision_condition are the first candidates) adds them without a new kind of thing.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Cluster, domain and boundary are names for one kind of thing, a container with an identity record, used in different practices.
fieldValues.rationale: Settled by precedent: the earlier rulings already make boundary and domain one thing, and a cluster has no property that distinguishes it. One way per goal.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A practice shows that a cluster, domain or boundary behaves differently in a way an added field cannot carry.
